classifications.rationale: FocusTrace does not currently check uniqueness of accesskey values.
FocusTrace validates role existence and ARIA properties but does not yet implement a dedicated host-element allowed-role expectation.
standards: WAI-ARIA role allowance on host-language elements

classifications.rationale: FocusTrace now checks exposed dialog and alertdialog semantics, including native dialog markup, for a usable accessible name and reports missing names as ARIA authoring warnings; its local AccName implementation remains deliberately bounded.
FocusTrace does not currently check role=text for focusable descendants.

FocusTrace now checks exposed treeitem roles for a usable accessible name and excludes descendant group subtrees from name-from-content evidence, while retaining warning semantics and a bounded local AccName implementation.
FocusTrace reviews heading level order but does not currently report headings solely because they have no discernible text.
FocusTrace does not yet report empty table header cells as a dedicated rule.

This rule verifies whether axe-core itself was injected into nested frames. FocusTrace uses its own local inspection architecture, so requiring the axe-core script would contradict the benchmark-only constraint.
FocusTrace reports skipped heading levels for REVIEW, covering the principal static ordering signal without claiming axe's full semantic ordering behavior.
FocusTrace validates whether images have an accessible name or are decorative, but it does not compare alt text with adjacent visible text for redundancy.
FocusTrace reports placeholder-derived naming and persistent-label risk; axe's rule covers a wider set of hidden/title-only labeling patterns, so only part of the authoring concern overlaps.
FocusTrace does not yet enforce top-level placement for banner landmarks.
FocusTrace does not yet enforce top-level placement for contentinfo landmarks.
FocusTrace validates native main hierarchy, overlapping top-level main-landmark placement but not every ARIA role=main case.
